nodes.content: Develop a semantic parser that generalizes variable binding and quantifier scope to unseen compositions without sacrificing familiar-construction accuracy.
requirements: Achieve ≥90% logical-form exact match on withheld scope–binding combinations with matched vocabulary and length distributions.
Keep familiar-construction exact-match accuracy within two percentage points of an equally sized supervised baseline.

nodes.content: Train a parameter-matched, typed scope-sketch decoder with de Bruijn binding and template-gated supervised fallback for familiar constructions.
Can the template gate distinguish withheld scope–binding combinations from familiar ones when vocabulary and sentence length are matched?
Typed scope–binder signatures will route ≥95% of withheld combinations to sketch decoding and ≥98% of familiar examples to fallback.
Construct vocabulary- and length-matched ScopeBind-Match splits; train the typed-signature gate; test ≥95% withheld-sketch recall and ≥98% familiar-fallback specificity.
Train the typed-signature gate on ScopeBind-Match and measure withheld-sketch recall and familiar-fallback specificity on matched test splits.
On ScopeBind-Match, the gate achieved 83% withheld-sketch recall versus the 95% target, despite 99% familiar-fallback specificity.
A novelty gate over canonical quantifier–binder graphs will achieve ≥95% withheld-sketch recall while retaining ≥98% familiar-fallback specificity.
Tune quantifier–binder graph-novelty gating on ScopeBind-Match development data; test withheld-sketch recall and familiar-fallback specificity against 95%/98% targets.
On ScopeBind-Match, graph-novelty gating raised withheld-sketch recall from 83% to 96% while retaining 98.4% familiar-fallback specificity.
Adopt graph-novelty gating: withheld recall improves 83%→96%, accepting specificity's 99%→98.4% drop while remaining above its 98% target.
Retrain the parameter-matched sketch/fallback parser using adopted graph-novelty routing; measure ScopeBind-Match withheld and familiar exact match versus baseline.
ScopeBind-Match v1 checkpoint and evaluation report with withheld and familiar exact-match scores against the parameter-matched supervised baseline.
Can de Bruijn sketches prevent binder capture in withheld inverse-scope nesting without eroding familiar-construction exact match?
Score withheld inverse-scope and familiar exact match for ScopeBind-Match v1 against the equally sized supervised baseline; annotate binder-capture errors.
ScopeBind-Match v1 scored 86% withheld inverse-scope exact match and 94% familiar versus 97% baseline; binder capture caused 38% of errors.
Decode compositional scope forests with capture-free binder instantiation and baseline-logit distillation on familiar constructions.
Implement capture-free scope forests, distill familiar logits, then test ≥90% withheld exact match and ≤2-point familiar-baseline gap on ScopeBind-Match.
Use the ScopeBind-Match v1 checkpoint and error report to implement capture-free scope-forest decoding with familiar-construction baseline-logit distillation.
ScopeBind-Match v2 checkpoint with capture-free scope-forest decoder and familiar-construction baseline-logit distillation.
Evaluate v2 versus v1 on ScopeBind-Match withheld exact match, inverse-scope binder capture, and familiar accuracy against the supervised baseline.
ScopeBind-Match v2 reached 91% withheld exact match, 96% familiar versus 97% baseline; binder-capture error share fell 38%→7%.
Adopt v2: 91% withheld exact match and 96% familiar meet targets; binder-capture error share falls 38%→7% versus v1.
Run a five-seed ScopeBind-Match audit comparing v1 and v2 exact match on distribution-matched withheld combinations and familiar constructions.
Five-seed audit: v1/v2 withheld exact match averaged 88%/91%; disabling v1-inherited sketch routing dropped v2 to 85%.
Are v2’s remaining withheld errors primarily incorrect rankings of valid scope forests rather than binder-instantiation failures?
≥60% of v2’s withheld errors have the gold scope forest in the top-five beam, ranked below an incorrect forest.
Decode top-five forests from the v2 checkpoint and classify withheld errors as ranking, missing-gold, or binder-instantiation failures.
Among v2 withheld errors, 38% misranked a top-five gold forest; 55% omitted gold; 7% involved binder capture.
Extend v2 with binder-safe, syntax-constrained scope-forest expansion and gold-coverage training while retaining familiar-logit distillation.
Can syntax-constrained expansion recover v2’s missing gold forests within 16 candidates while keeping familiar exact match ≥95%?
Initialize constrained v2 expansion from the v1 sketch-routing checkpoint; measure 16-candidate gold coverage and familiar exact match on ScopeBind-Match.
ScopeBind-Match: withheld gold-forest coverage rose from 94.4% (v2 top-five) to 97.1% (16 candidates); familiar exact match reached 95.8%.
Gold-coverage training on 16-candidate forests will raise withheld exact match to ≥93% while preserving familiar accuracy ≥95%.
Train 16-candidate gold-coverage loss with familiar-logit distillation; compare withheld and familiar exact match against v2 across five ScopeBind-Match seeds.
Five-seed ScopeBind-Match: coverage training reached 92.1% withheld exact match versus v2’s 91%, with 95.6% familiar accuracy.
Contrastive reranking of 16-candidate forests will raise withheld exact match from 92.1% to ≥93%, preserving ≥95% familiar accuracy.
Train contrastive forest reranking on ScopeBind-Match training splits; measure five-seed withheld and familiar exact match against the 92.1% coverage model.
Five-seed reranking raised withheld exact match from 92.1% to 93.4% and retained 95.3% familiar accuracy on ScopeBind-Match.
Adopt constrained reranking: 97.1% gold coverage; withheld match rises 92.1%→93.4%, with familiar accuracy 1.7 points below baseline.
Audit adopted reranker by sentence length and quantifier depth; verify 16-candidate gold coverage and ≥95% familiar accuracy on held-out ScopeBind-Match.
ScopeBind-Match audit report with held-out gold coverage, familiar exact match, and error counts by sentence length and quantifier depth.
Train a scope-graph parser with alpha-renaming equivariance and counterfactual quantifier-swap supervision, retaining familiar-logit distillation.
Can quantifier-swap counterfactuals change scope order without corrupting binder references in nested logical forms?
Independently verify ScopeBind-Match audit report's depth-stratified counts; measure counterfactual scope-graph parser's swap accuracy and nested binder-capture rate.
Independent audit reproduced depth-stratified counts; the scope-graph parser achieved 96% quantifier-swap exact match and 0.6% nested binder capture.
Use verified swap/capture results to refine alpha-equivariant scope-graph training; test nested binding, ≥90% withheld match, and ≤2-point familiar gap.
Implement the verified-swap refinement: train alpha-equivariant scope graphs with counterfactual swaps and familiar-logit distillation on ScopeBind-Match.
AlphaScope v1 checkpoint with alpha-equivariant scope-graph decoding, quantifier-swap training, and familiar-logit distillation.
Use typed CCG derivations with explicit scope-raising combinators and baseline-preserving residual adapters for familiar constructions.
Implement typed scope-raising CCG and residual adapters; evaluate ≥90% withheld exact match and ≤2-point familiar-baseline gap on ScopeBind-Match.
Train CCG adapters initialized from v2; stratify evaluation using audit counts and type-check derivations against AlphaScope graphs.
ScopeCCG v1 checkpoint and typed-derivation audit, with depth-stratified exact-match scores and AlphaScope graph-consistency checks.
Measure ScopeCCG v1’s withheld and familiar exact match, type-error rate, and depth-stratified accuracy against the 97% supervised baseline.
ScopeCCG v1 achieved 90.8% withheld and 96.2% familiar exact match versus 97% baseline, with 0.3% type errors.
Do ScopeCCG’s type-correct errors at quantifier depth ≥3 arise from scope-raising order or residual-adapter routing?
Ablate ScopeCCG v1 on depth-≥3 errors: independently oracle-fix scope-raising order and residual-adapter routing; compare exact-match recovery.
On a separate matched test, ScopeCCG scored 88.9% withheld and 94.4% familiar versus 97% baseline; scope-order/routing oracles restored 92%/96%, respectively.
At depth ≥3, scope-order correction will recover more withheld errors than adapter-routing correction; routing correction will recover more familiar errors.
Reconcile ScopeCCG’s initial 90.8%/96.2% with matched-test 88.9%/94.4%, then compare depth-≥3 scope-order and adapter-routing oracle recoveries by split.
Pre-register scope-order superiority on withheld errors and routing superiority on familiar errors before reconciling scores and rerunning audit-guided ablations.
Revised ScopeCCG v1 audit reconciling split-specific scores and documenting preregistered depth-≥3 scope-order versus routing oracle ablations.
Independently reproduce revised audit’s split-specific scores and test preregistered depth-≥3 oracle recoveries for withheld versus familiar errors.
Independent audit reproduced both splits; depth-≥3 order/routing oracles recovered 41%/18% of withheld errors and 12%/36% of familiar errors.
Defer ScopeCCG: initial 90.8%/96.2% passed, matched 88.9%/94.4% failed; target scope order (41% withheld recovery) and routing (36% familiar).
